Corporate.brandDescription: Strategy and operations consulting for mid-market enterprises that have outgrown boutique advice.
Corporate.mission: Mid-market companies are too small for the big firms' attention and too sophisticated for boutiques. We sit in the middle with strategic depth and operating discipline.
Corporate.vision: There's a clear opening for a mid-size firm focused on the strategy-meets-operations work that the giants over-bill and the boutiques can't scale.
coreValues: Trustworthy — a core principle the brand operates by.
Capable — a core principle the brand operates by.
Direct — we say what we mean without softening it.
Steady — a core principle the brand operates by.
Strategic — a core principle the brand operates by.
Corporate.scope:
Forum & Stack works across:
• Strategy plus operations
• Mid-market specialists
• Real scoping

Corporate.tagline: Strategy and operations consulting for large enterprises.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Blackwood is a surname with a senior, slightly institutional register. Strategy Group signals the firm category with the multi-discipline 'group' structure. The pair reads as a serious mid-to-large strategy firm with multi-discipline practices under one roof.
Corporate.manifesto: Blackwood Strategy Group is a multi-discipline strategy and operations consultancy serving large enterprise clients. The buyer is a CEO, CFO, or chief operating officer with a board-mandated initiative. The engagement is multi-year. The deliverable is operating improvement, measured.
Corporate.industrySummary: Large-enterprise strategy consulting is dominated by McKinsey, BCG, and Bain. The opening underneath them is for a serious mid-tier firm with operations depth and the long-engagement model required for transformation work — at a different price point and partner ratio.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Oliver Wyman (oliverwyman.com) is the closest peer. AlixPartners (alixpartners.com) holds the operations-heavy slot. L.E.K. (lek.com) sits in the strategy-mid middle. We sit in the regional mid-tier strategy-and-operations category.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Blackwood Strategy Group is a mid-tier strategy and operations consultancy serving large enterprises across multi-year transformation engagements.
Corporate.positioningRationale: We compete on partner ratio, engagement duration, and measured operating outcomes. The deliverable is operating-metric improvement, not deck count.

targetAudience.primary: CEOs, CFOs, COOs, and boards of $500M–$50B revenue enterprises with board-mandated strategy or operations initiatives.
behaviors: Report on transformation programs to boards quarterly.
Care about EBITDA improvement, working-capital release, and capability uplift.
motivations: Want a firm with operations depth and partner availability.
Want measured outcomes, not deck count.
Want a long engagement with continuity.

dos: Lead with operating outcomes, partner ratio, and engagement length.
Speak the language of CEOs and boards.
Publish a quarterly enterprise strategy benchmark.
Reference real CEO and CFO titles in case material.

messagingPillars.name: Strategy and operations under one roof
messagingPillars.description: Strategy formulation and operational execution under a single engagement team. The team that recommends is the team that helps deliver.

messagingPillars.name: Partner ratio
messagingPillars.description: Lower partner-to-engagement ratio than the top three firms. Partners are in the work, not at the steering committee.

messagingPillars.name: Outcomes in writing
messagingPillars.description: Engagements begin with written outcome targets — EBITDA improvement, working-capital release, capability uplift. Quarterly reviews measure against the targets.

Corporate.logoDirection: A serif wordmark — Blackwood set in a traditional book serif, with 'Strategy Group' beneath in tracked small caps. Used in proposals, board decks, and on the firm's office door.

typography.primary: A traditional book serif for the wordmark and board materials.
typography.secondary: A clean enterprise grotesque for working documents, dashboards, and reports.
typography.rationale: Tables and numbers tabular and disciplined.

Corporate.brandDescription: Tarrant Advisory Holdings operates a portfolio of professional services brands across management consulting, strategy advisory, and operational consulting categories.
Corporate.scope:
Tarrant Advisory Holdings works across:
• Multi-brand consulting operations
• Shared talent and partner network
• Cross-firm client coordination
• Compliance and quality across firms
• Annual investor and operator reporting
Corporate.mission: To provide a serious operating platform for mid-tier consulting brands that want to keep their identity and outsource the operations.
Corporate.vision: An advisory operator whose portfolio brands grow under their own names because the talent network and operations are shared.
coreValues: Senior — partners deal with partners.
Operational — talent and coordination run on schedule.
Reliable — predictable operations across firms.
Discreet — firm and client relationships stay private.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Tarrant is a real English surname-and-place with a heritage trade register. Advisory Holdings follows the multi-brand operator naming convention used in professional services (Marsh & McLennan Companies, AlixPartners' holding structure, Accenture's heritage advisory group structure). The pair reads as an institutional operator with multi-brand portfolio scale.
Corporate.manifesto: Tarrant Advisory Holdings owns and operates a portfolio of consulting brands. Each brand retains its identity, partner leadership, and client relationships; we operate the shared talent network, compliance, and back office. The buyer is a consulting firm founder considering sale, a major client seeking single-vendor consulting relationships, or an institutional investor holding consulting assets.
Corporate.industrySummary: Mid-market consulting has consolidated under a small number of multi-brand holdings (Marsh & McLennan, Accenture, AlixPartners). The opening underneath is for a regional mid-tier multi-brand operator.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Marsh & McLennan Companies (mmc.com) is the multi-brand consulting reference. AlixPartners (alixpartners.com) holds the multi-brand peer slot. Huron Consulting Group (huronconsultinggroup.com) sits in the multi-practice peer position. We belong in the regional mid-tier multi-brand consulting operator category.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Tarrant Advisory Holdings is a regional multi-brand consulting operator running talent, compliance, and shared operations across a portfolio of firms.
Corporate.positioningRationale: We compete on shared talent depth, cross-firm coordination, and operational reliability.

targetAudience.primary: Consulting firm founders considering sale, major clients seeking single-vendor consulting relationships, and institutional investors holding consulting assets.
behaviors: Care about partner retention, client renewals, and utilization.
motivations: Need an operator with shared talent network.
Need to keep firm identity post-acquisition.
Need a single-vendor multi-brand consulting relationship.

dos: Lead with firm portfolio, talent count, and client renewal rates.
Speak the language of firm founders, major clients, and procurement.
Publish quarterly operator letters.
Refer to firms by name, not by Tarrant tagging.
donts: No social media at the parent level.
No firm consolidation announcements without partner alignment.

messagingPillars.name: Multi-brand operator
messagingPillars.description: We own and partner with four to eight consulting firms across management, strategy, and operations categories. Each retains its identity.

messagingPillars.name: Shared talent network
messagingPillars.description: Centralized talent and partner network across the portfolio. Firms share access to senior practitioners and specialty expertise.

messagingPillars.name: Cross-firm coordination
messagingPillars.description: Coordinated client coverage across firms. Major clients can engage across firms through a single relationship.

Corporate.logoDirection: A serif wordmark — Tarrant set in a traditional book serif, with 'Advisory Holdings' beneath in tracked small caps. Used in contracts and the corporate office. Not used on consumer-facing firms.

typography.primary: A traditional book serif for the wordmark and corporate letters.
typography.secondary: A clean enterprise grotesque for operational reports.

Creative.tagline: A strategy firm built around the dissenting view.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Devil's Advocate is the real Catholic legal role (advocatus diaboli) appointed to argue against canonization in a saint's cause. Advisory is the plain category suffix. The naming sits in the literary-trade tradition.
Creative.manifesto: Most consulting firms sound like they wish they were the client. They mirror the company's language, soften the recommendations, and round off the edges. We made Outside Voice because the client already has internal voices. What they don't have is someone willing to say the thing nobody at the table will say. We say the thing. The brand is the function.
Creative.industrySummary: Consulting branding has been polished, neutral, and slightly cautious. There's room for a brand that's sharp, character-driven, and serious about saying what the client's internal team won't.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Brunswick Group (brunswickgroup.com) does the cautious-counsel peer. Strategy& (strategyand.pwc.com) holds the institutional middle. Public Digital (public.digital) sits in the modern design-led tier. We sit louder than any of them.
Creative.positioningStatement: An advisory firm that says the thing.

targetAudience.primary: 30 to 55. Founders, CEOs, and senior executives who have hired consultants and felt told what they already knew. They want someone who will disagree with them in writing.

dos: Disagree in writing
Quote the client's words and then the better answer
Talk like the advisor who has nothing to lose
donts: Soften the recommendation in the case study

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark in a punchy display serif with the V of VOICE stylized as a small speech-bubble flourish. Standalone speech-bubble icon for stickers, social profiles, and the back of every engagement letter.

colorPalette.name: Voice Red
colorPalette.usage: Primary brand color, hero surfaces, stickers

typography.primary: Migra for the wordmark and big display
typography.secondary: PP Neue Montreal for body and engagement letters
typography.rationale: Migra has personality and weight. Neue Montreal handles the readable bits. The pair feels designed and a little defiant.

customSections.title: What it isn't
customSections.body: Not a big firm. Not a mirror to the client. Not afraid of red. Not too cool to disagree with the CEO in writing.

customSections.title: Where it lives
customSections.body: Engagement letters that name the recommendation clearly and the disagreement clearly. Stickers in every welcome envelope. A small annual letter to past clients written like an opinion column. No client logos on the website.

Creative.tagline: A strategy firm that takes the second opinion seriously.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Counterview is a real but uncommon noun for an opposing assessment — single word, slightly literary. The definite article gives it the proper-noun register of an established firm.
Creative.manifesto: Most strategy consulting pretends to be the first opinion. Frameworks, transformations, north-star strategies. We started Second Opinion because the actual job is almost always the second opinion. The client has a view. They want it tested. We are the test. The firm is named after the actual transaction.
Creative.industrySummary: The 'second opinion' framing is an under-occupied position in strategy consulting. Most firms position as principal advisor; very few embrace the secondary-validator role. There is a real opening for a firm that takes the second-opinion frame as its identity.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Truth (truth.consulting) plays in the considered-small space. Redscout (redscout.com) holds the modern-boutique slot. Lab42 (lab42.com) is the peer in modern strategy. We sit further out — the brand is the request itself, sharply.
Creative.positioningStatement: Second Opinion is a strategy firm that does the second opinion well — fast, blunt, and on a fixed engagement.
Creative.positioningRationale: The brand stakes its position on the second-opinion role. Engagements are short, fixed-fee, and end with a written agree/disagree on the client's existing strategy.

targetAudience.primary: CEOs, founders, and boards already holding a draft strategy, who want it tested before committing.
behaviors: Use advisors to test, not generate.
Want a written opinion in weeks, not months.
Make decisions by consulting a small advisory circle.
motivations: Want a strategy tested fast.
Want a written agree/disagree.
Want a firm that does not pitch a full transformation.

dos: State agree or disagree directly.
Write the opinion as a one-page letter.
Reference the client's draft strategy explicitly.
Sign each engagement with the partner's name.

messagingPillars.name: Agree or disagree, on paper
messagingPillars.description: Every engagement ends with a one-page letter that states agree or disagree on the client's draft strategy, with the reasoning.

messagingPillars.name: Fixed fee, fixed length
messagingPillars.description: Engagements are six weeks, fixed price, published. No scope creep, no follow-on. The opinion is the deliverable.

messagingPillars.name: No follow-on
messagingPillars.description: We do not take the implementation work. The second opinion is the product. We hand the client back to their own team or to a different firm.

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark — The Counterview in a precise modern serif, with a small stamp-style mark indicating agree or disagree. The mark is the brand.

typography.primary: A precise modern serif for the wordmark and the letter.
typography.secondary: A neutral sans for working materials.
typography.rationale: The serif speaks. The stamp lands. The letter is what the client keeps.

Creative.tagline: A consulting firm where the whiteboard is the work.
Creative.brandDescription: The Whiteboard Co is a creative-led consulting firm that conducts all engagements in front of a physical whiteboard with the client, photographed and documented as the primary deliverable.
Creative.scope:
The Whiteboard Co works across:
• In-person consulting engagements conducted in front of a physical whiteboard
• Photographed whiteboard documentation as the primary deliverable
• Bound transcripts and photographs delivered after engagement
• Quarterly published essays on the whiteboard tradition
• Annual archive of whiteboard sessions
Creative.mission: To restore the whiteboard as the central object of strategy work rather than the deck.
Creative.vision: A consulting firm whose whiteboard sessions are remembered by clients across years.
coreValues: Specific — the whiteboard is the work.
Considered — every session is in person.
Warm — clients are at the board.
Literary — the writing about the whiteboard is part of the firm.
Creative.brandNameRationale: The Whiteboard is the foundational object of strategy and operations work — the surface on which problems are drawn, structures are sketched, and decisions are made. Naming the firm after the whiteboard stakes a clear position around the working session as the central work. The definite article + Co suffix follows the considered-creative trade-name school.
Creative.manifesto: Most consulting work ends in a deck the client reads alone. We started The Whiteboard Co because the actual most useful consulting moment is at the whiteboard — partners and clients together, drawing the structure, finding the answer. We work in front of the whiteboard; the photographs and transcripts are the deliverable.
Creative.industrySummary: Consulting deliverables have converged on PowerPoint decks. There is real space for a creative-led firm that explicitly positions on the in-person whiteboard session as the primary work.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Most boutique firms emphasize deliverables (decks, reports) rather than the working session. Forensic firms that work alongside clients in person play the closest peer space. We sit further out — the whiteboard session is the engagement.
Creative.positioningStatement: The Whiteboard Co is a consulting firm that conducts all engagements in front of a physical whiteboard with the client, with the photographed session as the primary deliverable.
Creative.positioningRationale: The brand competes on the whiteboard premise. Every engagement, every published essay, every deliverable is built around the working session.

targetAudience.primary: Decision-makers who want in-person working sessions rather than deliverable-focused consulting.
behaviors: Prefer in-person working sessions to deck reviews.
Care about the process of decision-making.
motivations: Want consulting at the whiteboard.
Want a firm with a working-session philosophy.
Want documented sessions as the deliverable.

dos: Lead with the whiteboard and the session.
Photograph the whiteboards.
Publish the quarterly essay on the whiteboard tradition.
Sign correspondence by the partner.

messagingPillars.name: Whiteboard sessions
messagingPillars.description: Every engagement is conducted in person, in front of a physical whiteboard, with the client present. The session is the work.

messagingPillars.name: Photographed documentation
messagingPillars.description: The whiteboards are photographed throughout the session. The photographs and a bound transcript are the deliverable.

messagingPillars.name: Quarterly essay
messagingPillars.description: The firm publishes a long-form essay on the whiteboard tradition every quarter — history, observations, drawings. The essay is the marketing.

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark — The Whiteboard Co set in a quiet display serif with a small illustration of a whiteboard frame beside it. The mark appears on bound transcripts and the firm's correspondence.
